mainTopic: Sources for טומאה of small and non-wool-or-linen fabrics, אביי and רבא on "או בגד", and how to reconcile the two teachings of דבי רבי ישמעאל.
overview: The גמרא asks where רבי שמעון בן אלעזר learns that a 3x3 handbreadth piece of שאר בגדים (fabrics other than wool and linen) can become טמא. The answer is a ברייתא that reads the extra word "או" in "או בגד". אביי uses that word to include a tiny 3x3 fingerbreadth piece of צמר ופשתים for טומאת שרצים. רבא learns that tiny piece from נגעים instead. The two argue back and forth about whether נגעים and שרצים can be learned from each other. אביי then says that two teachers of דבי רבי ישמעאל disagree. רבא answers that they agree, because one speaks of a small piece and the other of a big piece. The גמרא objects that רבא said the opposite earlier, and answers that either רבא retracted or the statement was really רב פפא's. A reading in רב פפא's name, that 'אף כל' is about כלאים, is rejected as a mistake (בדותא). רב נחמן בר יצחק then starts a new reading, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Where does he learn it from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the view that a 3x3 piece of שאר בגדים can become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where does he learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source. It wants to know which פסוק teaches that a 3x3 piece of other fabrics can become טמא. This line sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier discussion said that, in this view, a 3x3 piece of non-wool, non-linen cloth can receive טומאה. A ruling like that needs a basis in the תורה. So the גמרא now asks for it.

keyTerms.meaning: From where does he know it? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: From where does he derive it?
phrases.notes: He's asking where רבי שמעון בן אלעזר gets his view about a 3x3 piece in שאר בגדים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion earlier about 3x3 pieces of שאר בגדים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches that 3x3 of שאר בגדים is מקבל טומאה.

steps.title: It comes from the words "or a garment"
steps.stepSummary: The source is the extra word "או" in "או בגד", in the פרשת שרצים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is derived from "or a garment."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The source is the phrase "או בגד" ("or a garment") in the פסוק about שרצים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could simply have said "בגד". The extra word "או" ("or") is read as a רבוי, meaning a word that includes something extra. Here it includes items that would not normally count as a full garment.

keyTerms.meaning: It is derived / it comes out from

phrases.english: It is derived from "or a garment."
phrases.notes: The extra "או" is read as including something more.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question from step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase "או בגד" in the פרשת שרצים.

steps.title: A ברייתא that reads "or a garment" this way
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that "או בגד" teaches that a 3x3 piece of other garments can become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: "Garment" would teach me only a garment. From where do I know that a 3x3 piece in other garments is included? The verse says: "Or a garment."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that the תורה really does read "או בגד" this way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the word "בגד" alone would cover only a full garment. The extra "או" adds a 3x3 piece of שאר בגדים. This confirms that the derivation in step 2 is a known teaching, not a new idea.
steps.confusionAlert: In this ברייתא, the 3x3 measure for שאר בגדים is in טפחים (handbreadths). Later, the 3x3 for צמר ופשתים is in אצבעות (fingerbreadths), which is much smaller.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita:
"Garment" — I have only a garment;
three by three [handbreadths]
in other garments, from where [do we know it]?
The verse states: "Or a garment."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 2 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That "או בגד" includes 3x3 of שאר בגדים.
steps.whatToRemember: For the view that 3x3 of שאר בגדים can become טמא, the source is the extra "או" in "או בגד".

steps.title: What does אביי do with "or a garment"?
steps.stepSummary: אביי holds that שאר בגדים are not טמא at all, so the גמרא asks what he learns from "או בגד".
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי, what does he do with this "or a garment"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to אביי, who does not accept this teaching about שאר בגדים. It asks what he uses the extra words "או בגד" for. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumption is that no word in the תורה is extra. If אביי rejects the רבוי for שאר בגדים, he must use "או בגד" to teach something else. It is a clarifying question, not an attack.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he do with it? (what does he learn from it?)

phrases.english: And Abaye —
this "or a garment," what does he do with it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the other side (אביי) reads the same פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What אביי learns from "או בגד", given that he does not use it for שאר בגדים.

steps.title: אביי: it includes a small 3x3 piece of wool or linen
steps.stepSummary: אביי uses "או בגד" to include a 3x3 fingerbreadth piece of צמר ופשתים for טומאת שרצים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it to include three by three [fingerbreadths] of wool and linen, which becomes impure through creeping creatures.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that אביי uses "או בגד" for something else. It includes a tiny 3x3 fingerbreadth piece of wool or linen, which can become טמא through שרצים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A full garment would normally need to be bigger. אביי says the extra "או" teaches that even this small piece of צמר ופשתים counts for טומאת שרצים. So the word is not wasted, even though he does not use it for שאר בגדים.

keyTerms.meaning: Creeping creatures whose dead bodies give טומאה

phrases.english: He needs it to include
three by three [fingerbreadths] in wool and linen,
that it becomes impure through creeping creatures.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "או בגד" includes 3x3 fingerbreadths of צמר ופשתים for טומאת שרצים.

steps.title: רבא: we learn it from נגעים
steps.stepSummary: רבא does not need "או בגד" for the small wool or linen piece, because the תורה showed it for נגעים, and the same applies to שרצים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא: the Merciful One revealed it regarding leprous marks, and the same applies to creeping creatures.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבא knows the law about the small wool or linen piece without using "או בגד". He learns it from the laws of נגעים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה teaches clearly that a small 3x3 piece of צמר ופשתים counts as a בגד for נגעים. רבא says the same is true for שרצים. That leaves "או בגד" free to include שאר בגדים.

phrases.english: And Rava —
the Merciful One revealed it regarding leprous marks,
and the same applies to creeping creatures.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רבא does not need the derivation that אביי uses.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The small piece of צמר ופשתים is learned from נגעים, so "או בגד" is free for שאר בגדים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why one word in the פסוק can support two different teachings, depending on whether a second source is available.

steps.title: אביי: נגעים are stricter, so we cannot learn from them
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects learning שרצים from נגעים, because in נגעים even the threads of שתי וערב become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי: one can refute it. What about leprous marks? There, even warp and woof threads become impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why אביי does not accept רבא's comparison. נגעים have a special strictness that שרצים do not have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In נגעים, even loose threads (שתי וערב) can become טמא, which is not true for שרצים. Since נגעים are stricter, their small-size rule cannot be carried over to שרצים. So אביי still needs "או בגד" for the small wool or linen piece.

keyTerms.meaning: There is room to refute (the comparison)
What about ..., which has (a special strictness)?
Warp and woof (the threads of a weave)

steps.whatToRemember: אביי uses "או בגד" for a small 3x3 piece of צמר ופשתים in שרצים, because נגעים are too strict to learn from. רבא learns that piece from נגעים, which frees "או בגד" to include שאר בגדים.

phrases.english: And Abaye — there is room to refute:
What about leprous marks,
since even warp and woof become impure through them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's comparison in step 6, which supports אביי's reading in step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison that learns שרצים from נגעים.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: נגעים have a unique חומרא (שתי וערב become טמא), so their small-size rule cannot be applied to שרצים.

steps.title: רבא: The Torah wrote it by נגעים so we can learn שרצים from it
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues that if נגעים were stricter, the תורה should have written the rule by שרצים and let us learn נגעים from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one (רבא) says: If you think נגעים are stricter, the תורה should have written the rule by שרצים, and let נגעים be learned from them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back against אביי's claim that נגעים are stricter, so we cannot learn שרצים from them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's logic: the תורה writes a rule in the place that lets us learn it for the other case too. If נגעים were truly stricter, the תורה would have written the rule by the easier case, שרצים, and we would learn the strict case, נגעים, from it. Since the תורה wrote it by נגעים, it must want us to learn שרצים from נגעים.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (the other אמורא answers)
If it would enter your mind (if you were to think)
Let the Torah (the Merciful One) write
And let them come (be learned) from them

phrases.english: And the other one (Rava says):
If you think that leprosy is more stringent,
the Torah should have written it regarding creeping animals,
and let leprosy be derived from them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ: אִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ נְגָעִים חֲמִירִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא rejects אביי's objection from Step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: אביי's claim that שרצים cannot be learned from נגעים because נגעים are stricter.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: If נגעים were stricter, the תורה would have written the rule by שרצים and learned נגעים from there. The fact that it did the opposite shows that the rule is meant to carry over to שרצים.

steps.title: אביי: נגעים could not be learned from שרצים, because שרצים are stricter
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the תורה could not have written the rule by שרצים alone. שרצים have their own strictness: they make things טמא even at the size of a lentil.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one (אביי) says: נגעים could not be learned from שרצים, because one can challenge it: what about שרצים, which make things טמא even at the size of a lentil?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends his position. He shows that writing the rule only by שרצים would not have worked either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case has its own strictness. נגעים are strict because even the threads become טמא. שרצים are strict because a tiny piece the size of a lentil makes things טמא. Since neither case can be learned from the other, the תורה had to teach each one separately. This means רבא's proof from the placement of the rule falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: There is room to refute (to challenge the comparison)
What about X, which has this stricter feature? (the standard way to break a comparison)
The size of a lentil, the minimum size of a שרץ that makes things טמא

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think אביי is saying שרצים are stricter in every way. Each case is stricter in a different area. That is exactly why neither one can be learned from the other.

phrases.english: And the other one (Abaye says):
leprosy could not be derived from creeping animals,
because there is room to refute:
what about creeping animals,
which make one impure even with a lentil-bulk?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ: נְגָעִים מִשְּׁרָצִים לָא אָתוּ, דְּאִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: אביי rejects רבא's argument from Step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבא's claim that the תורה should have written the rule by שרצים if נגעים were stricter.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: נגעים cannot be learned from שרצים either, because שרצים are stricter in a different way (they make things טמא at the size of a lentil). So both had to be written.
steps.whatToRemember: The debate ends with each side holding its position. אביי says neither case can be learned from the other, so אביי needs "או בגד" for שרצים. רבא learns שרצים from נגעים.

steps.title: אביי: Two teachers from דבי רבי ישמעאל disagree
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that a ברייתא from דבי רבי ישמעאל, which uses "או בגד" to include all kinds of fabrics, disagrees with another teacher from the same school who limited things to wool and linen.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: This teacher of the school of רבי ישמעאל disagrees with another teacher of the school of רבי ישמעאל. For the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: "בגד" (garment) gives me only a garment of wool or linen. From where do we include camel hair, rabbit wool, goat hair, and the silks (שירין, כלך, סריקין)? The verse says: "או בגד" (or a garment).
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a ברייתא from דבי רבי ישמעאל that says all fabrics can become טמא. He explains that it clashes with another teacher from that same school, who said only wool and linen count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי holds that שאר בגדים do not become טמא, and he relies on a teaching from דבי רבי ישמעאל. But here another ברייתא from the same school uses "או בגד" to include all fabrics. אביי's answer is simple: these are two different teachers from that school, and they disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: A teacher of the school of רבי ישמעאל
I have only (the verse alone teaches only this)

phrases.english: Abaye said:
This tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael

phrases.aramaic: מַפֵּיק מֵאִידָךְ תַּנָּא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל.
phrases.english: diverges from another tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael.
For the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
"Garment" — I have only
a garment of wool or linen;
from where do we include
camels' hair and rabbits' wool,
goats' hair,
and the shirayin, the kalakh, and the serikin (silks)?
The verse states: "Or a garment."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הַאי תַּנָּא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל מַפֵּיק מֵאִידָךְ תַּנָּא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: how two teachings from the same school fit together.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to אביי, the two teachers of דבי רבי ישמעאל disagree. One includes all fabrics through "או בגד". The other limits things to wool and linen.

steps.title: רבא: No disagreement, because one is about a small piece and one is about a big piece
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the teacher who excluded שאר בגדים meant only a small 3x3 fingerbreadth piece. For a 3x3 handbreadth piece, he agrees it becomes טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: When this teacher of the school of רבי ישמעאל does not hold of שאר בגדים, that is only for three by three (fingerbreadths). For three by three (handbreadths), he does hold that it becomes טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer from אביי. He shows that the two teachings from דבי רבי ישמעאל do not actually disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teacher who excluded other fabrics was only talking about a tiny piece, 3x3 fingerbreadths. Only wool and linen become טמא at that small size. For a big piece of 3x3 handbreadths, every fabric becomes טמא. That fits the ברייתא that includes all fabrics through "או בגד", so both teachings agree.

keyTerms.meaning: Three by three fingerbreadths (אצבעות), a small piece
Three by three handbreadths (טפחים), a big piece

steps.confusionAlert: Look closely at the Hebrew. שָׁלֹשׁ (feminine form) goes with אצבעות, meaning fingerbreadths, a small size. שְׁלֹשָׁה (masculine form) goes with טפחים, meaning handbreadths, a big size. The whole answer depends on this difference.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer seems to clash with what רבא said earlier, that the תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל does NOT hold that 3x3 handbreadths of שאר בגדים becomes טמא. The next step raises exactly that contradiction.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי says the two teachers of דבי רבי ישמעאל disagree. רבא says they agree, because one is talking about a small piece (3x3 fingerbreadths) and the other about a big piece (3x3 handbreadths).

phrases.english: Rava said:
when he is not of the opinion,
this tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael,
regarding other garments, it is about three by three fingerbreadths;
three by three handbreadths, he does hold (becomes impure).

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: כִּי לֵית לֵיהּ לְהַךְ תַּנָּא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different way from אביי's in Step 10 to explain the two teachings from דבי רבי ישמעאל.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by size: each teaching is talking about a different size of fabric.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It looked like the two teachers of דבי רבי ישמעאל disagree about whether שאר בגדים become טמא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both agree. שאר בגדים are excluded only at the small 3x3 fingerbreadth size. At 3x3 handbreadths they become טמא.

steps.title: רבא contradicts what he said earlier
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that רבא himself said earlier that a 3x3 handbreadth piece of שאר בגדים is טמא according to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר but NOT according to the תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wait! Isn't it רבא who said that for a 3x3 piece of other fabrics, רבי שמעון בן אלעזר holds it can become טמא, and the תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל does not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's answer from step 11 by quoting something else רבא said, which seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 11, רבא said the תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל agrees that a 3x3 handbreadth piece of שאר בגדים becomes טמא. But earlier on the דף, רבא said this same תנא does NOT hold that way. So רבא appears to contradict himself.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds this / he does not hold this

phrases.english: But isn't it Rava who said
three by three [handbreadths] in other fabrics

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אִית לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar holds [it can become impure]

phrases.aramaic: לְתַנָּא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל לֵית לֵיהּ!
phrases.english: the tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael does not hold it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's answer in step 11 using another statement of רבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim in step 11 that the תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל agrees 3x3 handbreadths of שאר בגדים is טמא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Internal contradiction: רבא elsewhere said this תנא does NOT hold that 3x3 handbreadths of שאר בגדים is טמא.

steps.title: רבא changed his mind
steps.stepSummary: First answer: רבא retracted his earlier statement.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא took back that earlier statement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction simply: רבא changed his opinion and no longer holds what he said before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no real contradiction, because the earlier statement is no longer רבא's view. His final position is the one from step 11, which lets the two teachers of דבי רבי ישמעאל agree.

phrases.english: Rava retracted from that [statement].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Retraction: one of the two statements is no longer the speaker's view.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא abandoned his earlier view. Step 11 is his final position.

steps.title: Really it was רב פפא who said it
steps.stepSummary: Second answer: the answer in step 11 was actually said by רב פפא, not רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say instead: רב פפא is the one who said that answer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another way out: the statement in step 11 should be credited to רב פפא, so רבא never contradicted himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If two different אמוראים said the two statements, there is no contradiction at all. רב פפא was רבא's main student, so his words could easily be credited to his teacher.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say (introduces another answer)

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
Rav Pappa is the one who said this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, alternative answer to the contradiction in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-attribution: the statement belongs to a different speaker.
steps.terutzMaskana: Step 11's answer belongs to רב פפא, so רבא's own view stays consistent.

steps.title: רב פפא says the ברייתא is about כלאים
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא reads 'אף כל' in the ברייתא of דבי רבי ישמעאל as coming to include the laws of כלאים, not טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: 'So too all [garments mean wool and linen]' comes to include כלאים.
steps.whatsHappening: Here a new reading is given in רב פפא's name. The ברייתא that says unspecified 'garments' mean wool and linen is not about טומאה at all. It is teaching the law of כלאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא is about כלאים, it no longer clashes with the other ברייתא that includes all fabrics for טומאה. On this reading, only wool and linen mixed together count as forbidden כלאים.

keyTerms.meaning: So too all... (the generalizing phrase in the ברייתא)
Forbidden mixtures (here: wool and linen in clothing, שעטנז)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
'So too all' comes to include diverse kinds.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: אַף כֹּל, לְאֵתוּיֵי כִּלְאַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new way to read the other teaching of דבי רבי ישמעאל ('אף כל' = all garments mean wool and linen, from the previous amud), not the all-fabrics ברייתא quoted in step 10. This removes the dispute between the two teachers of דבי רבי ישמעאל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'אף כל צמר ופשתים' teaches that כלאים applies only to wool and linen.

steps.title: The Torah already says כלאים is wool and linen
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a דרשה is needed when the פסוק itself says 'שעטנז צמר ופשתים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But כלאים is written openly in the תורה: 'Do not wear שעטנז, wool and linen together'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב פפא: the Torah already says clearly that כלאים means wool and linen, so why would the ברייתא need to teach it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A דרשה should teach something new. Since the פסוק already names wool and linen, רב פפא's reading seems to make the ברייתא pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: A forbidden blend of wool and linen

phrases.english: Diverse kinds are explicitly written in it:
"You shall not wear diverse kinds,
wool and linen together"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב פפא's reading in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that 'אף כל' comes to include כלאים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule is already stated openly in a פסוק, so a דרשה is unnecessary.

steps.title: Needed for placing a garment on oneself
steps.stepSummary: Defense: without the דרשה we might think the wool-and-linen limit applies only to wearing. For merely placing a garment over oneself (העלאה), any two kinds might be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: that [limit to wool and linen] is only for wearing. But for placing on oneself, any two kinds are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב פפא. The פסוק only speaks about wearing, so the דרשה is needed for draping or placing a garment on oneself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'לא תלבש', which means wearing. Someone could think placing a garment over oneself follows a different rule and includes any two materials. The דרשה would teach that even there, only wool and linen count.

keyTerms.meaning: It would have entered your mind to say
Placing / draping a garment over oneself (not actually wearing it)

phrases.english: It would have entered your mind to say:
this applies [only] in the manner of wearing,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בְּהַעֲלָאָה כֹּל תְּרֵי מִינֵי אָסוּר.
phrases.english: but in placing [on oneself], any two kinds are forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 16 by finding a new case for the דרשה to teach.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finding a new case the פסוק does not cover (העלאה).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: For העלאה, any two kinds of material might be forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The דרשה teaches that even for העלאה, only wool and linen are forbidden.

steps.title: A קל וחומר makes the דרשה unnecessary
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the defense. If wearing, which benefits the whole body, is forbidden only for wool and linen, then placing a garment on oneself is surely not stricter.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't this a קל וחומר? Wearing benefits the whole body from the כלאים, and still you said only wool and linen are forbidden, nothing else. Placing a garment on oneself, all the more so!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the answer in step 17 using a קל וחומר. We would never have thought העלאה is stricter, so no דרשה is needed for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wearing is the bigger benefit, because the whole body enjoys the garment. If even wearing is limited to wool and linen, the lighter case of העלאה surely cannot forbid more materials. So the הוה אמינא of step 17 falls apart, and רב פפא's reading again has nothing to teach.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a lighter case to a stricter one (or the reverse)
Is it not all the more so?

steps.confusionAlert: The קל וחומר here works to make things more lenient: if the stronger case (wearing) only forbids wool and linen, the weaker case (העלאה) cannot forbid more.

phrases.english: But is it not an a fortiori inference?
Just as wearing, where one benefits
with his whole body from the diverse kinds,
you said wool and linen, yes,
anything else, no.
Placing, is it not all the more so?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the defense offered in step 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The הוה אמינא that העלאה might forbid any two kinds of material.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A קל וחומר from לבישה already shows that העלאה cannot be stricter, so no דרשה is needed.

steps.title: רב פפא's statement is a mistake
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the statement credited to רב פפא is a fabrication and was never really said.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the statement of רב פפא is a mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on רב פפא's reading entirely and says it must be a wrongly reported teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the ברייתא would teach nothing new about כלאים, the reading cannot be right. Instead of defending it further, the גמרא rejects the report that רב פפא said it at all.
steps.whatToRemember: The attempt to read 'אף כל' as being about כלאים fails: the פסוק already says it, and the קל וחומר covers העלאה. So the version credited to רב פפא is called a בדותא.

phrases.english: Rather, that of Rav Pappa is a mistake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the final conclusion from the failed defense in step 18.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב פפא's reading of the ברייתא as being about כלאים is rejected as a בדותא.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק starts a new reading
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק begins his own explanation of 'אף כל' in the ברייתא. It continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: 'So too all...'
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. רב נחמן בר יצחק is about to give a different topic that the ברייתא's 'אף כל' might refer to, and his explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After רב פפא's reading was thrown out, a new אמורא tries again. Like רב פפא, he will say the ברייתא is not about טומאה, but he will point to a different area of law.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
So too all...

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר: אַף כֹּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב פפא's reading is rejected, a new approach to the same ברייתא begins.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Begins a new reading of 'אף כל'. The content continues on the next amud.
